inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: Organizers say 8 million people attended more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, but there’s no official count, so that figure should be treated as their estimate—not a verdict from the country. Protests are part of civic life; they don’t override elections or the constitutional limits that protect everyone. The language of “defending democracy” may rally opponents of President Donald Trump, but it shouldn’t be used to portray ordinary political disagreement as a threat to vulnerable people. In a republic, lasting change comes through lawful institutions and persuasion, not claims that the loudest crowd speaks for the nation.
